turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Hi, thanks — ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?

"Honestly, I went to bed around 11, but that's my second sleep of the day, if that makes sense — I'd finished my last night shift that morning and already had a stretch of sleep after work before picking up my daughter."
Thanks for explaining that. Approximately how many total hours did you sleep across both of those sleeps in the last 24 hours? And would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

"About seven hours total, in two pieces — maybe four right after the shift and then a shorter nap in the afternoon before daycare pickup. I'd say I slept okay, not great — it's never one solid stretch, so I don't feel as rested as if it were all together, but it's enough to function."
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? And why did you choose to do that activity?

"Just scrolled through my phone a bit, honestly — nothing productive, just messages and stuff. I do it because after four in a row it's the one bit of downtime that's mine before I have to be 'on' for my daughter."
Thanks for sharing that. Over the past two weeks, what factors have most affected your sleep quality?

"Honestly, the shift rotation is the big one — every time I flip back to nights it throws things off for the first day or two. Otherwise it's just the usual, my daughter waking up in the night sometimes and me being the one who hears it even though I'm not technically on 'day person' hours. Not much has really changed though, it's the same pattern it's been for a while now."
Thanks, that makes sense. Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days, or not so much? Why?

"Not so much, if I'm being honest — it's fine, I get enough hours to function, but it's never really restful because it's always split. I don't think about it too much day to day, it's just kind of the deal with this job, but every now and then I wonder what it's doing to me long term."
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

"Honestly? Not really, no — I mean, I hit seven, sometimes close to eight if you add it all up, but split like this it doesn't feel like the same thing as one solid stretch would. So the number's fine, it's more that nobody tells you it matters how you get there, not just how much."
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep in one solid stretch, given your current schedule and responsibilities?

"Honestly, having my partner handle mornings makes the biggest difference — if he's got our daughter, I'm not being woken up early. The hard part is my body just doesn't stay asleep that long on its own, even with the curtains and white noise, so it splits itself into pieces whether I plan it that way or not."
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?

"Yeah, honestly, I do — it's kind of the one wind-down thing before I try to sleep, even though I know it's probably not helping. After a night shift I'm usually too wired to just lie there, so scrolling is more of a habit at that point than an actual choice."
Thanks for explaining that. Do you regularly use social media? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?

"Yeah, I'm on there — mostly just scrolling, nothing intentional, honestly. It's more the last hour before I even attempt sleep, not really planned use, just kind of autopilot scrolling until my eyes get heavy."

Thanks, that’s clear. Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar apps?

If yes, when did you start using them, and what do you mainly use them for (for example, work, study, personal questions, or something else)?

"Yeah, actually I do — I started maybe a year or so ago, I think it was ChatGPT first. I mostly use it for random stuff, like double-checking something for work schedules or if I need to write an email quick, nothing too deep."
Thanks, that’s helpful. Since you’ve been using social media and AI chatbots regularly, do you feel like your sleeping habits have changed at all compared to before you used them?

"Not really, honestly — my sleep's been rough since I started this job, way before I was on my phone or using ChatGPT much. I don't think either of those changed anything, they're more just what I do while I'm already lying there awake anyway."
That makes sense. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?
"Honestly, getting a real block of it after the shift instead of it splitting into two — even just once a week would feel like a win at this point."
Given your work, family, and other daily responsibilities, do you think getting that solid block of sleep after a shift is actually doable? Why or why not?

"Honestly? Not really — well, maybe once in a while if I'm lucky and my daughter sleeps in or my partner takes her out for the morning. But most days there's just too much going on — nursery drop-off, stuff around the house — so it splits whether I want it to or not."
"I'm 34, work as a logistics coordinator, born in Kraków, and still living here — never really moved."
Thanks for sharing that. Before we wrap up, is there anything else you’d like to add about your sleep, your schedule, or anything we talked about today?
